narration:
The fire has burned down to its embers, and the ash-quarry behind you exhales the day's heat in slow, invisible breaths. Ossa does not look up when you sit. She has the guard's habit of watching a man by the edges of her attention — the set of his shoulders, where his hands go — and she keeps it up while she works a whetstone along a blade that hardly needs it.

"Kaelen," you say. "Kaelen Vurr."

The whetstone stops. It is a small sound, that stopping, but in the hush of the Verge it carries like a dropped coin. She looks at you properly for the first time since you crested the rim — scar tissue pulling one cheek into a permanent half-squint, road-dust gone grey in the creases of her neck. "Three days on the same fire and you finally cough it up." She says it flat, without triumph. "Most men lie sooner. You just didn't say anything at all. That's rarer." She spits into the ash, then nods once, which from her appears to be the whole of a ceremony. "Ossa. You knew that. Now we're even."

Something shifts in you as she says *even* — not a warmth, nothing so kind. A settling. You have spent your life on the near side of things, watching, tallying, waiting for the arithmetic to resolve before you commit; and the habit has a weight to it that you have never been able to name until now, when a very small piece of it comes off. A name is nothing. A name is the cheapest thing a man owns. But it is the first thing you have given away here instead of counted, and the ledger you carry in your chest registers it the way still water registers a stone — a ring moving outward, a line drawn on the side of the page that has always been empty. You do not feel stronger. You feel *entered*.

Across the embers, Ossa returns to her blade. "Road east forks past the slagfields," she says, as if resuming a sentence from an hour ago. "Left goes to Kaldrath's outriders. Right goes somewhere nobody signs for. You'll want to know which before the wagons roll, and I'd want to know why you're asking, but I've got a rule about that." The whetstone starts again. "One name a night. You spent yours."

skill_mastery_changes.note: For the first time, an entry falls on your own side of the page — a thing given rather than observed and priced.
Sitting close enough to feel the shape of another's wariness soften teaches you the texture of it.

new_entities.name: The Slagfields Fork
new_entities.description: A split in the eastern ash road past the slagfields: left toward Kaldrath's outriders, right toward an unregistered route Ossa declines to describe.

narrative_memory_updates.note: Kaelen gave Ossa his true name — the first thing he has volunteered to anyone in Vaeltharion — and she considers them square; she keeps a one-question-a-night rule.
